correctness.rationale: For an admissible rank array, every composite minor condition is stable under the vertex diagonal torus acting by change of bases. A generic one-parameter subgroup gives pairwise distinct weights on the arrow matrix-unit basis of H, so fixed points in projective PH are precisely coordinate points. At a point with exactly one nonzero rank-one arrow all products of length >=2 vanish, so membership in PΩ_r is equivalent to r_{i,i+1}>0 on that arrow. Fixed locus therefore has exactly sum_{i:r_i,i+1>0} d_i*d_i+1 points. Compactly supported Euler characteristic of complex algebraic C*-varieties localizes to the fixed locus even if singular; projectivity identifies χ_c with χ_top. If all direct bounds zero the projectivization is empty. Independent toy example V0=V1=V2=C with both direct bounds1 but composite bound0 gives XY=0 in P1: two points, χ=2. Formal localization, not the toy case, proves all dimensions.
